whatIs.title: What is the JSON ↔ CSV Converter?
whatIs.description: A two-way converter for JSON and CSV formats aimed at developers. Use it to turn a REST API's JSON response into a spreadsheet-ready CSV, or convert CSV data exported from Excel into a JSON array. It handles nested JSON objects, custom delimiters, header inclusion, and other options you need in real-world workflows.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Choose JSON to CSV or CSV to JSON.
2. Paste text or choose the file encoding before opening a file.
3. Set delimiter, header, nesting/array or number options, then convert.
4. Inspect the table and statistics, then copy or download the same complete result.

items.q: How are nested JSON values converted?
items.a: Flattening uses dots and array indices in column names and reports name collisions. Preserving nesting writes objects and arrays as JSON strings.

items.q: Are codes such as 00123 and large integers preserved?
items.a: CSV values remain strings by default. Numeric conversion is opt-in. JSON integers outside the safe range are rejected; enter large identifiers as quoted strings.

items.q: What are the file and data limits?
items.a: Original file bytes and decoded UTF-8 text are each limited to 2 MiB. Limits are 10,000 data rows, 200 columns, 200,000 cells, JSON depth 20, and 8 MiB each for the intermediate table and output. Failed conversion preserves the input.

items.q: Can the tool output EUC-KR files?
items.a: EUC-KR applies to file reading only. Output is UTF-8, with an optional BOM for CSV only. The file encoding setting does not change pasted text.
